entities.name: At4g32460 BIIDXI
observations: Arabidopsis DUF642 cell-wall protein; also called BDX and reported as BIDXII in one seed-endosperm study.
Overexpression increased total pectin methylesterase activity during germination and improved germination; antisense and SALK lines reduced leaf PME activity and produced short, seedless siliques.
Protein interacted in vitro with the catalytic domain of AtPME3/At3g14310, but an in-vivo complex or direct catalytic mechanism was not established.

Expression was detected in imbibed embryos, roots, leaves, stems, stamens, and petals; auxin and nematode-responsive localization support broader developmental regulation rather than proving PME control.

entities.name: At3g14310 PME3
observations: The catalytic domain interacted in vitro with BIIDXI/DUF642 proteins in the reported germination study; definitive in-vivo partnership was not demonstrated.

entities.name: BIIDXI pectin remodeling
observations: bdx-1 mutants showed altered homogalacturonan methyl-esterification, scarce unesterified homogalacturonans in endosperm during embryo bending and mature seeds, and misshapen embryos.
Thermopriming increased PME activity in wild type but not bdx-1, supporting BIIDXI-dependent PME-associated remodeling; this remains genetic/physiological evidence.

entities.name: BIIDXI auxin development
observations: bdx-1 seedlings had longer hypocotyls, auxin accumulated in mutant epidermal cells, and PIN1 distribution differed; evidence supports an auxin-efflux mechanism for hypocotyl elongation, not direct PME regulation in that experiment.

entities.name: PMID:25442819
observations: Primary study linking BIIDXI/DUF642 proteins to PME activity, germination, and reproductive development.

entities.name: PMID:29137987
observations: Primary study linking bdx-1 to embryo morphology and homogalacturonan methyl-esterification during seed development.

entities.name: PMID:36432778

entities.name: 2-part intertrochanteric fracture
observations: For a stable, well-reduced fracture, conventional fixation uses a sliding hip screw with a standard side plate.

entities.name: Sliding hip screw
observations: A standard sliding hip screw construct for a stable 2-part intertrochanteric fracture conventionally uses a 4-hole side plate with four cortical screws; extra cortical screws, variable-angle plates, and locking constructs are not routinely required.

entities.name: Four-hole standard fixation
observations: Conventional teaching identifies four side-plate screw holes as the standard construct for stable, well-reduced 2-part intertrochanteric fractures.

entities.name: Two-hole clinical evidence
observations: A 2-hole sliding hip screw plate can have similar clinical outcomes to a 4-hole plate in stable fractures, but biomechanical testing favors 4 holes; a systematic review recommended reserving 2-hole plates when a 4-hole plate cannot be used.
